data.narrative:
Electric Air is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Chris Mui and Jeremy Osbourne. The valuation analysis draws from a comparables universe of 9 private peers (including Helion, Redwood Materials, and Electric Hydrogen) and 1 public comparable (LNZA), though the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints to support a reliable peer-median approach.

Only the Stage-Progression method is applicable to this valuation. Using the company's $500K total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to the next stage, this method implies a valuation of $1.25M. The Peer-Median approach was not applied due to insufficient narrow-set comparables—while 9 Climate & Energy peers exist, none fell into the same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier buckets required for robust triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.06M to $1.44M, with a median point of $1.25M. This reflects early-stage valuation mechanics tied directly to recent capital deployment rather than revenue or operational scale. Key uncertainties include the availability of tighter peer comparables at this specific stage and the appropriate stage-progression multiple for frontier climate technology (which may differ from the 2.5x baseline applied here). Additional data on customer traction or technical milestones would strengthen conviction in this range.
